name: Natters
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village on the Sonnenplateau, featuring the Natterer Weiher lake and a stunning view of the Innsbrucker Nordkette.
beschreibung:
Overview

Natters is situated on a sun-drenched plateau of the Southern Mittelgebirge at an altitude of 783 meters, roughly 200 meters above the Inn Valley and merely five kilometers southwest of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck. Belonging to the Innsbruck-Land district, this appealing community counts around 2,115 residents across 7.33 square kilometers, bordering directly on neighboring Mutters. The elevated terrace affords breathtaking panoramas across the rugged limestone crags of the Innsbruck Nordkette, the Martinswand cliff, and the dramatic Kalkkögel peaks. Natters effortlessly blends traditional Tyrolean village idyll with instant access to Innsbruck's urban culture and education, while the renowned Lake Natters (Natterer See) establishes it as a premier destination for tranquil outdoor recreation and award-winning camping. The municipality belongs to the Innsbruck region.

History

Archaeological finds confirm continuous human habitation on the Natters terrace since the Bronze and Iron Ages, highlighted by Roman burial discoveries such as the 1st-century 'Dead Man in the Wine Vessel'. The earliest written record dates to 1151 as 'Naters' in a deed by the Counts of Andechs. During the 13th century, Castle Sonnenburg served as a territorial court, while the historic Waidburg manor in the village center was constructed around 1518 as a hunting retreat for Emperor Maximilian I, functioning today as the municipal hall. Lake Natters was originally created around 1480 by Archduke Sigismund the Rich as a ducal fishpond. The parish church of St. Michael preserves a 15th-century Gothic choir, richly redecorated in Rococo style by master builder Franz Singer in 1754. A major milestone arrived in 1904 with the inauguration of the Stubaitalbahn, the world's first single-phase alternating current railway.

Getting There

Transport links to Natters are outstanding, offering fast connections paired with scenic mountain vistas. By car from Innsbruck, drivers take the A13 Brenner Autobahn to exit Innsbruck-Süd (Mutters-Natters), or follow the toll-free country road L227 in just ten to fifteen minutes. A memorable journey is provided by the historic Stubaitalbahn narrow-gauge tramway (line STB), departing directly in front of Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof and winding leisurely through meadows and woods to Natters and Lake Natters in approximately 25 minutes. Regional VVT bus routes 404 and 4140 run frequent daily schedules, while cyclists can comfortably reach the village from Innsbruck via Mentlberg by e-bike.

Tips

The crown jewel of the community is the Lake Natters Holiday Resort (Ferienparadies Natterer See), an internationally acclaimed holiday and camping resort featuring a 3.5-hectare natural moor swimming lake, sandy beaches, a 66-meter water slide, and an extensive inflatable aquapark. A beloved excursion destination for families is the traditional Natterer Boden inn, set upon a peaceful forest clearing, boasting authentic Tyrolean dining, an adventure playground, and a heritage farm with rare domestic animal breeds. A scenic tram ride aboard the nostalgic Stubaitalbahn offers panoramic valley views for all ages. A village stroll reveals historic landmarks including the Waidburg, St. Michael's Rococo parish church, and painted Tyrolean farmhouses.
